components.cost_effect: Five separately identified derivative operations per step, with possible shared computation.
components.goal: Estimate the exact joint vector field without an inverse-Hessian estimator.
components.key_estimate: Eqs. (7)–(10) identify these as unbiased estimators of Dz,Dv,Dx, not generally of grad h away from z*,v*.
components.name: Shared component pair at the old state
components.operation: Use the same uniform G index and F index in all three directions, and evaluate every derivative at the old joint state.
components.requires: Finite sums and the five component derivative operations described in the variant.
transfer_checks: Recheck sampling weights if sampling ceases to be uniform.
Recheck the vector-field identity and regularity if the model or derivative oracle changes.
Establish tracking and convergence independently before attaching a performance theorem.

limitations.statement: No rate, accuracy complexity or admissible rate-certified step-size window is extracted. Proposition 2.1 is a deterministic zero-direction lemma, not an Algorithm performance theorem.
The x direction targets Dx at the current states; it is not asserted to be an unbiased hypergradient at inexact inner or auxiliary states.

variants.cost: Per iteration: one sampled G index and one sampled F index; separately charge one G z-gradient, one G inner Hessian-vector product, one G mixed-derivative-vector product, one F z-gradient and one F x-gradient. Products need not materialize matrices. State storage is 2p+d scalars, excluding model/autodiff workspaces; arithmetic for vector sums and updates is O(p+d). Over T iterations each of the five derivative operations is evaluated T times. Shared computation can reduce runtime but does not make these operations free or establish an unrestricted Oracle Complexity bound.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p.3 Algorithm 1; p.4 Section 2.1, Eqs. (10a)–(10c)
variants.name: SOBA finite-sum core rule
variants.output: Generated trajectory and terminal state (z^T,v^T,x^T). Algorithm 1 has no explicit return instruction; terminal state describes the result of its T updates, not a source-certified stationarity output selector.
public_inputs: Positive integers p,d,n,m; component functions G_i and F_j
Initial states z0,v0 in R^p and x0 in R^d
Positive integer horizon T and supplied positive step-size sequences rho_t,gamma_t for 0<=t<T
variants.query_and_update: At iteration t use the old state (z^t,v^t,x^t). Draw i uniformly in [n] and j uniformly in [m], independently of one another and of prior sampling conditional on the current history. With the same pair for all directions, query a=grad_1 G_i(z^t,x^t), b=G_11,i(z^t,x^t)v^t, c=G_21,i(z^t,x^t)v^t, d1=grad_1 F_j(z^t,x^t), d2=grad_2 F_j(z^t,x^t). Set Dz^t=a, Dv^t=b+d1, Dx^t=c+d2. Simultaneously set z^(t+1)=z^t-rho_t Dz^t, v^(t+1)=v^t-rho_t Dv^t, x^(t+1)=x^t-gamma_t Dx^t. Never substitute a newly updated state into another direction in the same iteration.
variants.requirements: F=(1/m)sum_j F_j and G=(1/n)sum_i G_i. Required component gradients and second-derivative-vector products must exist at queried states and be available. Inner strong convexity and implicit-differentiation regularity are needed for the intended bilevel interpretation; defining the update itself does not supply convergence hypotheses.
variants.state_and_initialization: Initialize arbitrary z0,v0,x0. No history table or full component pass is required by this rule.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Run exactly T iterations with the supplied sequences. Algorithm 1 treats these sequences as inputs; this record specifies no convergence-certified tuning, accuracy stopping rule or convergence rate.

use_restrictions: Reference covers the executable rule with user-supplied step sizes, not a convergence guarantee.
Resource accounting describes this selected implementation, not unrestricted Oracle Complexity.
Independent review and publication have not been performed.

summary: Single-loop simultaneous updates of inner, linear-system and outer states using one shared pair of independently sampled component indices; no performance theorem attached.
title: SOBA joint-state algorithm (rule and component contract)
use_when: Implement the SOBA direction rule without estimating a Hessian inverse.
